observed_title: Norm-induced Cuts: Outer Approximation for Lipschitzian Constraint Functions

read_ranges.scope: Entire 29-page text, including all definitions, proofs, computational examples, references, and Appendices A/B. Original PDF pages 5, 11, 12, 13, 17, 27, 28, and 29 were rendered to inspect cut, convergence, complexity, big-M, and packing formulas.

topic_relevance.A02: direct: the paper constructs an outer relaxation from global Lipschitz bounds and norm-induced distance cuts; proves set inclusion, feasibility and optimality limits, gives packing/covering termination bounds and error-dependent oracle complexity. The framework assumes a global optimizer oracle for each relaxed subproblem and does not provide a closed-form subproblem solver.

definitions.name: Problem model and Lipschitz data
definitions.statement: Minimize a continuous f over a nonempty compact domain Ω⊂Fⁿ subject to componentwise r(x)≤0, where r:Ω→Rᵐ is globally Lipschitz with known constant L>0 under the chosen domain/output norms; the output norm must be monotonous.

definitions.name: Norm-induced cut
definitions.statement: For an infeasible y∈Ω, the cut is ||r(y)₊||/L ≤ ||x−y||. It removes a norm ball around y; validity uses the global Lipschitz bound and monotonicity of the output norm.

definitions.name: Relaxed outer set Q_k
definitions.statement: Starting from Q₀=Ω, Q_k is Ω intersected with the k norm-induced cuts centered at previous infeasible oracle solutions. The paper’s key invariant is Q⊆Q_k.

definitions.name: ε-approximate feasibility and geometric constants
definitions.statement: The paper defines ε-approximation by every residual component r_q(x)≤ε, without an objective-gap requirement. It defines domain radius ρ(Ω) and asphericity α(Ω) for oracle-complexity bounds.

theorem_cards.label: Lemma 3.3 (outer-relaxation inclusion)
assumptions: Every prior center x_i is infeasible and lies in Ω.
r has a valid global Lipschitz constant L; the output norm on Rᵐ is monotonous.
theorem_cards.statement: For every k, the true feasible set Q={x∈Ω:r(x)≤0} is contained in Q_k. Therefore infeasibility of a relaxed problem certifies infeasibility of the original problem, and a relaxed optimum is a lower bound on the original minimum.
proof_steps: 作者证明：for feasible x̄ and infeasible center x_i, restrict to indices where r_p(x_i)≥0; since r_p(x̄)≤0, the componentwise magnitude of r(x̄)−r(x_i) dominates r(x_i)₊.
核验基础推导：monotonicity gives ||r(x_i)₊||≤||r(x̄)−r(x_i)||≤L||x̄−x_i||, which is exactly the cut; doing this for every center yields Q⊆Q_k.
gaps: This direction fails if L is underestimated or the output norm lacks the required monotonicity.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 3.4 (feasibility and accumulation points)
assumptions: Q is nonempty; Ω is compact.
Each relaxed problem is solved exactly enough to return a point in Q_k; cuts use the valid global Lipschitz constant.
theorem_cards.statement: NIC either returns an actually feasible point in finite time, or produces a sequence with a convergent subsequence and every accumulation point is feasible for the original problem. No objective optimality is asserted by this theorem.
proof_steps: 作者证明：if the method stops, its explicit residual check r(x_k)≤0 gives feasibility.
If it runs indefinitely, compact Ω supplies convergent subsequences. Assuming a limit x* is infeasible, continuity gives a strictly positive violation norm near the subsequence tail.
Each later iterate must lie outside the cut ball centered at an earlier iterate, so tail points are separated by more than a fixed positive radius; this contradicts convergence of the subsequence.
核验基础推导：the contradiction uses both the cut lower bound ||r(x_i)₊||/L≤||x_j−x_i|| and the Cauchy property of a convergent subsequence.
gaps: An infinite run is allowed. Feasibility is only shown for accumulation points, not for every finite iterate.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 3.6 (optimality of limits with global master solves)
assumptions: Every relaxed master problem P_k is solved to a global optimum.
The continuity/compactness conditions of Theorem 3.4 hold.
theorem_cards.statement: If the method terminates with a feasible point, it is globally optimal. If it runs infinitely, every accumulation point of its exact global-master solution sequence is globally optimal.
proof_steps: 作者证明：Q⊆Q_k implies the restricted-master optimum is a lower bound on the true minimum.
At finite stopping the point is also feasible for Q, so the lower bound and feasible objective coincide.
For a convergent subsequence, feasibility follows from Theorem 3.4; continuity of f passes the restricted optimum values to the limit, while each remains below the true optimum.
核验基础推导：a feasible limit has value at least the true minimum, while the limit of global relaxed values is at most that minimum; equality follows.
gaps: If masters are only locally solved, this global-optimality conclusion is unavailable; the paper’s Example 5.2 exhibits convergence to a poor feasible limit.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 3.9 (locality under local master solutions)
assumptions: Each P_k returns a local optimum.
The algorithm stops at a point that passes the exact original feasibility check.
theorem_cards.statement: The returned feasible point is locally optimal for the original problem. If the method runs indefinitely, accumulation points need not be locally optimal.
proof_steps: 作者证明：a neighborhood where x_k minimizes over Q_k also contains the smaller local feasible set Q∩Bε(x_k), since Q⊆Q_k.
核验基础推导：the local objective minimum over the superset is attained at x_k, and x_k belongs to the original local feasible set; therefore no nearby feasible point has a lower objective.
gaps: Only finite stopping gives the local-optimality conclusion.

theorem_cards.label: Theorems 4.5–4.6 (oracle-complexity bounds)
assumptions: The exact theorem statements additionally rely on the surrounding complexity setup: f and r Lipschitz, Ω has nonempty interior, and an optimizer lies with the prescribed interior margin.
The domain is finite-dimensional Rⁿ; ε-approximation means residual feasibility only.
For the upper bound, ρ(Ω) is the radius of a containing norm ball.
theorem_cards.statement: The cited lower bound is T(ε)≥c/[α(Ω)^n ε^n] for some c>0; the paper proves T(ε)≤((2ρ(Ω)+ε)/ε)^n. At fixed n the bounds have the same ε^{-n} order. The upper bound is authors’ result; the lower bound is quoted from reference [45].
proof_steps: 作者证明上界：a maximal ε-packing of queried points yields an oracle-count bound by the volume ratio vol(Ω+εB/2)/vol(εB/2).
Contain Ω in a ball of radius ρ(Ω), compare volumes of the expanded and small balls, and simplify to ((2ρ(Ω)+ε)/ε)^n.
作者援引 [45] 得到下界；未在本文证明。
核验基础推导：the volume scaling vol(tB)=t^n vol(B) yields the stated upper bound once the packing/covering lemma applies.
gaps: The lower-bound constant c and derivation are imported from the cited complexity text. The theorem is a residual-feasibility oracle bound, not an ε-optimal objective-value guarantee.

constant_dependence.explicit: Each cut radius is ||r(x_i)₊||/L. For infeasible instances, δ=min_{x∈Ω}||r(x)₊||>0, so distinct oracle points have pairwise distance >δ/L and T is bounded by a packing number. The volume argument gives T≤vol(Ω+(δ/L)B/2)/vol((δ/L)B/2). For ε-feasibility, the paper gives an upper bound ((2ρ(Ω)+ε)/ε)^n and cites a lower bound c/[α(Ω)^n ε^n].
constant_dependence.dependence: L must be a valid upper Lipschitz constant: larger valid L weakens cuts; underestimating L can exclude feasible points and invalidates Q⊆Q_k. The complexity bounds depend on dimension n, domain geometry (packing/covering, ρ, α), and ε. Component-specific constants may improve or worsen cut radii relative to a vector-valued bound depending on violation and tightness.

endpoint_limits.feasible_case: A feasible problem may run forever; only all accumulation points are guaranteed feasible, and globally optimal only if each relaxed master is solved globally.
endpoint_limits.infeasible_case: Compactness and continuity make minimum violation δ>0; the algorithm cannot revisit a point and finite packing/covering bounds imply termination, though the bound is geometric and can be large.
endpoint_limits.approximation: ε in the complexity analysis controls each constraint residual r_q(x)≤ε. It is not by itself a bound on |f(x)−f*|.
endpoint_limits.oracle_and_norm: The approach assumes an oracle can solve each nonconvex relaxed problem to global optimality for Theorem 3.6. Norm cuts can be reverse-convex; p=1 or ∞ can be reformulated as mixed-integer linear constraints only with valid big-M bounds, and p=2 produces nonconvex quadratic constraints.

reusable_methods.method: Retain every prior infeasible incumbent as a norm-induced exclusion cut, with a globally valid Lipschitz constant, and maintain the invariant Q⊆Q_k.
reusable_methods.transfer: This is a certificate of outer relaxation only if the norm monotonicity and L bound are valid. When using a numerical/approximate Lipschitz bound, inflate it upward rather than risk understating it.

reusable_methods.method: Separate feasibility convergence from objective optimality: compactness plus cuts ensure feasible accumulation points; global solution of every relaxed master upgrades them to global optima.
reusable_methods.transfer: Do not treat a feasible limit from local subproblem solutions as optimal. Exact finite stop, asymptotic limit, and ε-residual stop have different guarantees.

reusable_methods.method: Use packing numbers for infeasible termination and volume ratios for finite-dimensional bounds; use ε-coverings when the ambient field supports a finite cover.
reusable_methods.transfer: The paper’s complexity formulas depend on domain geometry, dimension, and residual scaling; state the oracle model and geometry constants explicitly.

reusable_methods.method: For separately known component Lipschitz constants, use the largest violated-component radius at the current point.
reusable_methods.transfer: The authors show the componentwise method can be better or worse than the vector map; compare radii instead of assuming more constants always accelerate convergence.

unchecked: All 29 PDF pages including both appendices were read. Original PDF pages 5, 11–13, 17, and 27–29 were rendered with PyMuPDF; the norm-cut, inclusion/convergence proofs, oracle bounds, and 1/∞-norm MILP encodings were visually inspected.
The numerical examples were not rerun. The cited lower-complexity theorem (Nemirovski–Yudin) and citations used for Lipschitz constant estimates were not independently reproved.

Independent derivation checks cover the set-inclusion inequality, the accumulation-point contradiction, the global-optimality squeeze, and the volume-ratio upper bound; broader oracle-complexity lower-bound conditions remain sourced rather than independently verified.
